scientific_hypothesis: A geometric progression thickness template (ratio r∈[1.08,1.12]) with 85nm HfO2 upper bound will produce candidates with higher UV transmission by pre-filtering absorption-dominated thick-HfO2 configurations, enabling the optimizer to focus computational budget on stopband engineering within feasible transmission windows.
expected_advantages: Systematic chirp gradient improves visible/NIR rejection bandwidth
Initialization template guides optimizer toward physically feasible region
known_risks: Geometric constraint may limit optimal thickness combinations
85nm HfO2 cap may reduce stopband depth if insufficient optical thickness
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should show improvement in stopband rejection (300-1100 nm) compared to route_01 while maintaining comparable passband transmission, and tightest_margin should not degrade across rounds.
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will remain below route_01 due to HfO2 absorption in the 255-280 nm passband, visible in reduced valid_candidates count.
thicknesses_nm should show monotonic or graded progression if the chirp optimization converges, rather than uniform quarter-wave values.
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best.
If mean transmittance in 255-280 nm falls below 0.6 for three consecutive rounds, flag HfO2 absorption risk and stop, keeping the current best for comparison.
